title: A letter to the head teacher
text:
Class 4B
Cempaka Primary School
3 February

Dear Mrs Wulan,

We are writing to ask you to put a water refill station in our school playground.

At the moment, many pupils bring drinks in plastic bottles and throw them away after one use. Last week, our class counted the plastic bottles in the school bins. In just five days, we found 214 bottles! We think this is far too many.

A refill station would help in several ways. Firstly, there would be less plastic rubbish. Plastic bottles can take hundreds of years to break down, and some of them end up in rivers and the sea. Secondly, families would save money, because pupils could bring the same bottle every day. Finally, it would help everyone to drink more water, which keeps our bodies and brains working well.

Some people might say that a refill station would cost too much. However, our class has a plan. We will hold a cake sale every Friday for a month to help pay for it, and we have asked the parents' committee to help too.

We believe a refill station is the best idea our school could have this year. Please could we visit your office to show you our plan? We would be happy to answer any questions.

Yours sincerely,
Class 4B
